content.comment_body: Hello all, I am seeking advice on an unusual networking issue. I need to forward ports 80 and 8080 on my ISP-provided router, but cannot select my [product_name] from the device list, even though it is online and its custom webpage is accessible. Networking seems fine—pinging works and everything is reachable—yet the router fails to recognize it as online. I noticed in [product_name] [product_name] software under FILE > PROPERTIES > GENERAL that the device name field is disabled. I can't assign a device name; it remains greyed out no matter what I try. Could naming the device help it appear in the network? Any advice?

A device name typically can only be set in network mode, not in diagram mode. However, I doubt the missing device name is why you can't see your [product_name] on the network. If you don't plan to connect the [product_name] to another network, remove the gateway address. If you don't use a DNS server, deselect “Customize DNS Server” and remove the DNS server address. In my experience, [product_name] modules appear on the network even without device names, gateway, or DNS information.

Thanks for your response. I just performed a factory reset on the [product_name], configured only IP and subnet, and skipped other settings. Everything is functioning—the device can be pinged and [product_name] software locates it. However, my ISP router still doesn't recognize it, so this seems like a router issue. I’ll give it another half hour in case it’s a network polling delay; otherwise, I will test a different router setup and bridge my modem/router.
Still no luck—my ISP modem/router does not see the [product_name] as online, although it clearly is. I will try swapping out the router.

I'm unfamiliar with ISP modem/routers. For reference, I use a Fritz!Box and a network switch. My setup includes multiple [product_name] modules, [product_name] panels, and other controllers, without issues.

The ISP modem/router manages port forwarding using device names primarily, with IPs as a secondary option. The problem is that I can’t assign a device name to my [product_name] due to the greyed-out field. As a result, I’ll need to switch to a different router.

I don't believe the 'device name' in [product_name] software has the same meaning as a network-visible device name. You can try this: open a blank network project, right-click in the network view, select 'Import', and import your diagram. After importing, click the gear icon and you should be able to edit the device name.
That solution works for the network project name, but switching back to the diagram tab, the name field remains greyed out and empty.
Agreed—I’ll go ahead and purchase a new router. Problem solved.

Did you finish testing with the network project? Try transferring the network project diagram, including the device name, to your [product_name]. If the router can detect it after transfer, that could be the solution.
I tried that and waited about 20 minutes for network polling, but unfortunately it didn’t work.
You didn’t mention you had already done that, so I couldn’t have known.
Thank you very much for your assistance.

Thanks again for your support. Replacing the router resolved the issue—the ISP router lacked flexibility and customization. After configuring the new one, I could remotely access my [product_name] with port forwarding. Reconnecting my other Wi-Fi devices will take more time.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face challenges when their [product_name] device doesn't appear online in the ISP router’s admin panel, despite being network accessible. The main frustration is the inability to set a device name via [product_name] software, which users believe is required by the router to manage port forwarding through device identification. Attempts to modify the name are blocked by a disabled field, and peers suggest that this may not actually map to a network-visible name. In the end, the root cause appears to be the router's method of detecting devices, prompting the user to replace the hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to assign a network-visible device name to their [product_name] using dedicated software, so that the device is properly recognized in the router interface for configuring port forwarding.
